intro: This is the story of one household that became a family name. It begins with a man called Bdo (Bedros) on the high plain of Karin, follows his descendants across a closing frontier in 1829–1830 to Lake Khanchali, and gathers every Bdoyan the records name, from his time to ours.
toc: A New Home on Lake Khanchali
Afterword: How This History Could Be Written
ref_intro: Everything behind the story: the sources used, every source still to be read online and on paper, a step-by-step guide to completing the family tree, and the words and names you will meet in the records. Every web address is a link.
sheets_p: The research handbook (see Download below) has four sheets to print and fill in: your line back to Bdo, a family group sheet, “where our branch lives today”, and a research log.

c.lead: This is a working edition, and every Bdoyan can add to it: your branch and where it lives today, a story, a photograph or document, a correction, or help with the records. Choose what you want to send, fill in what you know, and the page will write it as a message for you to send.
c.kind: What would you like to send?

branch: who you descend from and where your family lives
correction: something in the book that is wrong

c.f_house: Which house or line do you come from?
c.h_ancestor: Name, and dates or place if you know them, e.g. “Hovhannes, son of Mesrop, born about 1890 in Pokr Khanchali”
c.f_village: The family village before it moved
c.f_today: Where the households of your branch live today
c.h_today: One line each: town, country and number of households, e.g. “Yerevan, Armenia, 3 households”. No street addresses.
c.h_what: e.g. “Photo of Mesrop and Anush, about 1912” or “Birth certificate of my grandfather”
c.n_attach: Attach the photo or scan to the email or WhatsApp message when you send it.
c.h_where: Chapter and page, or the sentence

helps.yerevan: Visit the National Archives in Yerevan
helps.tbilisi: Visit the National Archives in Tbilisi
helps.elders: Record the elders of my branch

c.h_text: Write as much as you like, in Armenian, Russian or English.
c.h_relation: e.g. “grandson of Grigor Bdoyan of Pokr Khanchali”
c.h_contact: Only the compiler sees this. It is never published.
c.f_credit: In the book, credit me as
c.consent: I agree that what I send may be used in the family book and on this page
c.living: Anyone living who is named here has agreed
c.out_p: Send it to the compiler of the book. Copy it into an email or a chat, or use one of the buttons.
c.out_note: Nothing is published until the compiler has checked it. The code at the end of the message lets the compiler add your entry to this page exactly as you wrote it.
c.wall_empty: Contributions appear here once the compiler has checked them. Be the first to add your branch.
c.owner_p: Contributions saved here are private until you approve them. Paste a message you received to add it.
